milestones.label: Matthews et al., 1987
milestones.title: Methane emission from natural wetlands: Global distribution, area, and environmental characteristics of sources
milestones.note: This study develops a global wetland database at a 1-degree resolution by integrating vegetation, soil, and inundation data to estimate global methane emissions

milestones.label: Keppler et al., 2006
milestones.title: Methane emissions from terrestrial plants under aerobic conditions
milestones.note: This is a brief report published in Nature discussing methane emissions from terrestrial plants under aerobic conditions, with no abstract available in the provided text.

milestones.label: Prigent et al., 2007
milestones.title: Global inundation dynamics inferred from multiple satellite observations, 1993–2000
milestones.note: This study presents a global estimate of monthly inundated surface areas from 1993 to 2000 using a multisatellite approach combining passive microwave, scatterometer, and optical data

milestones.label: Lai et al., 2009
milestones.title: Methane Dynamics in Northern Peatlands: A Review
milestones.note: This paper is a review of methane dynamics in northern peatlands

milestones.label: Gauci et al., 2010
milestones.title: Woody stem methane emission in mature wetland alder trees

milestones.label: Dlugokencky et al., 2011
milestones.title: Global atmospheric methane: budget, changes and dangers
milestones.note: This review paper examines the global atmospheric methane budget, radiative forcing, and emission sources, highlighting the need for improved observation networks and isotopic measurements to constrain emissions at regional and global scales

milestones.label: Olefeldt et al., 2012
milestones.title: Environmental and physical controls on northern terrestrial methane emissions across permafrost zones
milestones.note: This study compiled a database of growing-season methane emissions across northern permafrost zones to assess environmental and physical controls

milestones.label: Bridgham et al., 2013
milestones.title: Methane emissions from wetlands: biogeochemical, microbial, and modeling perspectives from local to global scales
milestones.note: Wetlands represent the single largest natural methane source globally, but significant uncertainties remain due to poor integration of microbial controls and transport mechanisms into process-based models.

milestones.label: Kirschke et al., 2013
milestones.title: Three decades of global methane sources and sinks
milestones.note: This study presents a global synthesis of methane sources and sinks over three decades, but no abstract is available to provide further methodological or regional details.

milestones.label: Pangala et al., 2013
milestones.title: Trees are major conduits for methane egress from tropical forested wetlands
milestones.note: Tree stems emit substantially more methane than peat surfaces, accounting for 62-87% of total ecosystem methane flux.

milestones.label: Turetsky et al., 2014
milestones.title: A synthesis of methane emissions from 71 northern, temperate, and subtropical wetlands
milestones.note: Wetland methane emissions are driven by soil temperature and water table in swamps and bogs, but these relationships are strongly modified by wetland type, region, and disturbance history.

milestones.label: Pangala et al., 2017
milestones.title: Large emissions from floodplain trees close the Amazon methane budget
milestones.note: This study investigates methane emissions from floodplain trees in the Amazon to reconcile regional methane budgets
